transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because… even when I’m having what I’d call a better day, when I’m trying to keep to myself and do normal things, I can’t seem to shake this feeling that certain people are watching me. Mostly people at church, and some from the walking club too. It’s like they’ll say something that sounds ordinary to everyone else, but I can tell there’s a little message in it about me.

And the church bulletin too — I know it probably sounds strange, but I’ll read a line in there and it feels like it’s been put in on purpose, like it’s referring to me or something I did or thought. I’ve tried telling myself it’s just a coincidence, but it keeps happening, or at least it feels like it keeps happening. It makes it hard to relax around people because I’m sitting there wondering what they know, or why they’re bringing it up that way.
Do you believe for certain that those people are sending messages about you?

I don’t know if I’d say “certain” every single second, because there’s a part of me that tries to be reasonable about it and says, maybe I’m reading too much into things. But when it happens, it feels very real to me. Like at church, someone will make a comment, or I’ll see something in the bulletin, and I get this strong feeling that it was put there for me to notice — like they’re hinting at me without saying my name.

And the walking club too… it’s not everybody, but certain people, certain things they say, the way they look over or talk around me. I can’t shake the feeling that they’re watching me or that they know something about me. So I guess I’m not saying I have proof, exactly, but in the moment it feels like, yes, they are sending little messages about me.
Have you ever heard a voice when no one else was there?

Yes… I have, though I feel a little embarrassed saying it because it doesn’t happen like in a movie or anything. It’s more when the house is really quiet, like if I’m sitting in the living room or doing dishes, and I’ll hear my name called from the kitchen or maybe from the porch.

Sometimes it’s just my name, and sometimes it’s a few words, like someone said something short. What makes it odd is that it sounds like my friend’s voice — clear enough that I’ll actually answer back, like, “What?” or I’ll turn toward where it came from. And then I remember nobody is there, or I’ll check and there’s no one in the kitchen, no one outside.

It’s not constant, but it has happened more than once, and it’s unsettling because for that second I really think somebody spoke to me.
Have these experiences made it harder for you to manage your usual work, home responsibilities, or relationships?

Yes… I mean, I still live at home, and I can manage some things, so it’s not like I’m completely unable to function. But it has definitely made my life smaller, if that makes sense.

I used to go to quilting gatherings more regularly, and I really enjoyed that — it was one of the things that got me out and around people. But I’ve stopped keeping up with it. I’ll tell myself I’m just skipping this week, and then it turns into several weeks. Same with the walking club. I used to like the routine of it, seeing familiar people, getting exercise, but now I don’t go much, because it feels uncomfortable and I come home feeling worn out from just trying to act normal.

Even my gardening has fallen off, and that bothers me because I used to take pride in the yard. I still do a little bit here and there, but not like before. Things get left too long.

My daughter has noticed, I think. She’s been checking on me more often — asking if I’ve eaten, reminding me about appointments, that kind of thing. She tries to be gentle about it, but I can tell she’s worried. I don’t like needing that, but I suppose I do need more help than I used to.
How long have these experiences been going on?

It’s been… close to a year, I think. Not quite a full year, but about eleven months now.

At first I thought it was just stress or me being tired, and I didn’t really keep track of it like, “this is the day it started.” But looking back, the voices, and feeling like there were messages meant for me, and even just having trouble keeping my thoughts straight sometimes — that’s all been going on for around eleven months. It sort of crept up on me, and then after a while I realized it wasn’t just a bad week or two.
Have you been neglecting your personal hygiene, like bathing or changing clothes less often than you used to?

I’m not really sure I’d say I’ve been neglecting it, no. I mean… I still bathe and change my clothes. Maybe I’m slower about getting going some mornings, and if I’m not leaving the house I might stay in the same comfortable clothes longer than I used to, but I don’t think I’ve stopped taking care of myself in that way.

My daughter hasn’t said anything like that to me either, and she probably would, gently, if she thought I looked unwashed or something. I try to keep myself decent. It’s just more that everything feels like it takes more effort than it should, but I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped bathing or anything like that.
Do other people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that your thoughts seem jumbled?

Yes… my daughter has said that a few times, though she tries not to make me feel bad about it. She’ll say, “Mom, I’m not following you,” or “Can you start that over?” And I can tell from people’s faces sometimes that I’ve lost them.

It’s like I start out trying to explain one simple thing — maybe something about the mail that came, or something I heard mentioned at church — and in my mind it all feels connected. But then while I’m talking, I’ll suddenly be on quilt patterns, or the birds outside, or how something felt like a warning, and by the time I look back at the person, they’re just sort of staring at me. Then I realize I haven’t actually said the part that would make it make sense.

It’s embarrassing, because I don’t always notice it while it’s happening. In my head there’s a path between the thoughts, but I guess I don’t say all the steps out loud, or I take too many turns. Sometimes I’ll stop and say, “Wait, what was I trying to tell you?” and that bothers me. I used to be better at keeping to the point.
Before this past year began, had you always been someone who felt uncomfortable being close to people or tended to have unusual beliefs that others found odd?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t think I was always that way, not in some big obvious sense.

I mean, I’ve probably never been the most outgoing person in the room. I’ve always liked having some quiet time, and I’m not someone who makes a dozen new friends everywhere I go. But I had people I was close to, and I could be friendly, and I don’t remember people acting like I was strange all the time or anything like that.

As for unusual beliefs… I don’t know. I’ve always had my own way of looking at things, I suppose, like anybody does. And I was raised to pay attention to signs in life in a more ordinary way, you know, like feeling something was meaningful or feeling guided sometimes. But I don’t remember other people telling me before all this that my beliefs were odd or that I made them uncomfortable.

So… no, I don’t think that was just how I always was. At least not that I noticed.
For at least one full month, have you been having these experiences most days?

Yes… yes, it’s definitely been more than a month. I wish I could say it was just a short stretch, but it’s been going on since not too long after my close friend died — that was about a year and five months ago now.

At first I thought maybe it was just grief making everything feel strange, and I kept telling myself it would settle down after a few weeks, then after a few months. But it didn’t really stay that brief. These experiences have been there most days for a long time now, not every single minute, but often enough that it feels like it’s been part of my daily life since around then.
